messages:
maria: Anyone else hitting a weird rate-window desync in the sample app? I see bursts of 429s even though tokens in the pool look fine. repro on both js and py SDKs.

jordan: Huh — can you paste quick repro steps + logs? which sample app flags?

maria: Steps: start sampleapp with higher concurrency, paginate an embed endpoint, rotate tokens quickly.

maria: Minimal repro:
```bash
./run-sampleapp --concurrency=12 --rate-window=60
# in another terminal
for i in {1..300}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" "http://localhost:8080/embeds?page=$((i%5))"; done
```

maria: log shows weird window values:
```
2026-03-20T14:23:10Z ERROR rate: window_sync_mismatch id=worker-3 expected=60 observed=8
2026-03-20T14:23:10Z WARN  client: token-refresh race for user=acct-42
```

sam: I think this is the old parity gap: js-sdk uses a sliding token-bucket aligned to system clock, py-sdk used an internal tick-based leaky bucket. When pagination cursors cause bursts + auth refresh, the window calc drifts.

lee: Yep. We saw similar in staging a month ago but assumed env mismatch. Does the sample app bring its own rate/window config or inherit from SDK default?

maria: It uses SDK defaults unless overridden. I tried forcing identical config in both SDKs and still reproduced, so it's likely a coordination race w/ the local window reset on token refresh.

jordan: Can you confirm whether the client-side window resets on 401/refresh or we keep the remaining bucket? That difference would explain the spike.

sam: Quick note: js-sdk currently resets currentWindowRemaining=windowSize on refresh (intent was to avoid negative buckets). py-sdk decrements but preserves remainder. So under backpressure + refresh you get either spike (js) or smoothing (py).

maria: Ugh. That explains it. For onboarding docs we should call out this behavioral difference. People will use sampleapp and think server is flaky.

lee: Temporary mitigation: enable "smoothing=true" in sampleapp config or use staggered token refresh (add small random jitter). Example:
```json
{"rate_window_align": "none", "smoothing": true, "refresh_jitter_ms": 200}
```

jordan: I'll open a PR to the sampleapp to set smoothing on by default for the quickstart, and add a deterministic test to reproduce the condition (control concurrency + force token rotations).

ci-bot: Created issue #4123: "client window reset parity => sampleapp 429 bursts" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/issues/4123)

maria: thx. Can we also add a short note in SDK parity docs that refresh semantics differ and recommended flags? Onboard customers will miss this.

sam: Agree. I'll draft a short blurb and link to the issue. Also propose we add an opt-in API param like `preserve_window_on_refresh` to both SDKs for explicit behavior.

lee: For production-facing SDKs we should default to preserving the remainder (safer) and make reset an explicit opt-in for low-latency microburst use cases.

jordan: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/789 (adds smoothing default + repro harness).

maria: Verified locally with PR branch — bursts gone with smoothing enabled. Adding it to quickstart reduces confusing 429s. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Linked PR #789 to issue #4123

maria: Ok closing this thread — follow-ups will happen in GH issue. Thanks all. :pray:
